documents.spec.md:
# Spec Kit Delivery v1

Build the user-approved standalone public extension for Codex and Spec Kit 1.0.12.

- FR-001: Map requirements, acceptance criteria, and tasks to an approved baseline.
- FR-002: Execute CLI, API, UI, and inspection scenarios with observable assertions.
- FR-003: Preserve failed attempts, bound repairs to three cycles, and reject stale evidence.
- FR-004: Generate L0/L1/L2 browser and editable PowerPoint presentations from one source.
- FR-005: Require separate human GitHub approval and protected CI for final acceptance.
- FR-006: Install independently and alongside Agentstandards without changing its architecture gate.
- FR-007: Distribute source publicly while keeping raw demonstration evidence local or in access-controlled storage.

- AC-001: Missing, duplicate, modified, skipped, and failed evidence cannot pass verification.
- AC-002: CLI, API, UI, and inspection success/failure fixtures exercise real execution.
- AC-003: Browser and PowerPoint preserve content, evidence links, images and speaker notes.
- AC-004: Agent, stale, dismissed, or unauthorized reviews cannot approve completion.
- AC-005: Clean Spec Kit 1.0.12 installation exposes all six commands and the wrapping preset.
- AC-006: No v1 completion claim until this repository has passed real human acceptance.
- AC-007: Public-repository CI never uploads raw command output, HTTP bodies, screenshots, traces, speaker notes, or presentations; any published attestation contains only non-sensitive hashes, identifiers, and pass/fail metadata.
documents.plan.md:
# Approved implementation direction

The user approved the original Spec Kit Delivery plan in this conversation on 2026-09-26 and
changed the distribution repository from private to public on 2026-09-29. This revision records
the changed scope for review; it is not a fabricated GitHub baseline approval.

Use a deterministic Python CLI, strict versioned schemas, Git/source fingerprints, and append-only
baseline/run directories. Execute project commands with timeouts, HTTP checks with httpx, UI checks
with Playwright, and text inspections against repository files. Use a shared presentation content
model for HTML and editable PowerPoint export. Keep generated evidence outside source control.
The public source repository is a distribution channel: users clone or install the extension, while
raw CLI output, HTTP responses, screenshots, traces, speaker notes, and presentations remain local
or in explicitly configured access-controlled storage. Public CI may publish a sanitized attestation
containing hashes, identifiers, provenance, and pass/fail metadata, but no raw demonstration content.

Read human authority from live GitHub APIs and trusted default-branch policy. Separate agent
barthisagent from human approver bbjwz. Keep privileged auditing on the default branch and never
execute candidate code in that job. Use the unprivileged review event only as a wake-up signal.

Bootstrap the trust root through a separate human-reviewed PR, then pin that reviewed runner revision.
The public repository must use secret scanning, push protection, default-branch protection, and a
protected audit environment. A public evidence path fails closed when it would upload raw evidence;
trusted acceptance consumes a non-sensitive attestation and the human reviews detailed evidence
locally or through separately authorized private storage. Missing requirements keep delivery
unaccepted. No automatic merge or deployment.

scenarios.title: Delivery regression suite
scenarios.expected: All unit and execution integration tests pass.

scenarios.title: Clean Spec Kit installation
scenarios.expected: All commands, preset and workflow install in a clean project.

scenarios.title: Incomplete acceptance remains visible
scenarios.expected: The report documents that live human acceptance is pending.

scenarios.title: Public CI publishes no raw demonstration evidence
scenarios.expected: Public-repository CI retains raw evidence locally or privately and publishes only a non-sensitive verification attestation.

narrative.problem: Agents can claim completion without demonstrating the agreed work.
narrative.expected_benefit: Expected to improve review discipline; business benefit is not measured.
narrative.implementation: Baseline mapping, execution evidence, shared deck content, and GitHub approval gates.
narrative.operations: Use synthetic data, preserve failures, keep raw evidence local or private, publish only non-sensitive attestations, and require trusted CI and human acceptance.
limitations: Real acceptance remains pending; local fixtures do not prove human sign-off.
Detailed evidence is not published from the public repository; reviewers need local access or separately authorized private storage.
